1.title: Probes, Health Checks and API Deprecations
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Probes, Health Checks and A P I Deprecations. It covers the exam area Application Observability and Maintenance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Implement probes and health checks. Understand A P I deprecations. Practice with six hands-on labs worth thirty-seven points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Observability and Maintenance (fifteen percent). Practice in this module: six labs, thirty-seven points, about forty minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Three probes, three questions
1.text: Three probes, three questions. The figure shows this: What each probe decides. Exam tip: A failing readiness probe removes the Pod from the Service endpoints; a failing liveness probe restarts the container.

1.title: Three probes, three questions, continued
1.text: Three probes, three questions. The kubelet checks the health of a container with probes. A container is "running" as soon as its process starts; that says nothing about whether the app works. Startup. Question: has the app finished starting? What a failure does: after failure Threshold failures the container is restarted; the other probes are paused until it succeeds. Readiness. Question: can the app take traffic now? What a failure does: the Pod is removed from the Service endpoints (not restarted); it returns when the probe passes. Liveness. Question: is the app still alive? What a failure does: the container is restarted.

1.title: Three probes, three questions, continued
1.text: Three probes, three questions. Liveness is for apps that hang. Readiness is for apps that start slowly, warm a cache, or lose a dependency for a while. A slow starter needs a startup probe, so that the liveness probe does not kill it during start.

1.title: Probe mechanisms
1.text: Probe mechanisms. H T T P get. Passes when: the response status is two hundred to three hundred ninety-nine. Example: H T T P get path slash healthz, port eighty eighty. T C P socket. Passes when: the T C P connection opens. Example: T C P socket port five thousand four hundred thirty-two. exec. Passes when: the command exits with zero. Example: exec command cat, slash temp slash healthy. G R P C. Passes when: the G R P C health check answers serving. Example: G R P C port nine thousand ninety. Exam tip: An H T T P probe passes with a status code from two hundred to three hundred ninety-nine; an exec probe passes when the command exits with zero.

1.title: Probe mechanisms, continued
1.text: Probe mechanisms. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Probe mechanisms, continued
1.text: Probe mechanisms. initial Delay Seconds. Meaning: wait before the first probe. Default: zero. period Seconds. Meaning: how often to probe. Default: ten. timeout Seconds. Meaning: how long one probe may take. Default: one. success Threshold. Meaning: passes in a row to count as success (must be one for liveness and startup). Default: one. failure Threshold. Meaning: failures in a row to count as failed. Default: three.

1.title: Probe mechanisms, continued
1.text: Probe mechanisms. A liveness probe that is too strict (a one-second timeout on a slow app, a check of a dependency) causes restart loops. Make the liveness check cheap and local. Probes are set per container; you cannot change them on a running Pod: edit the Deployment (Pods are replaced) or recreate the Pod.

1.title: Reading probe failures
1.text: Reading probe failures. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Pod that is Running but zero slash one Ready has a failing readiness probe: read the events with kube control describe pod.

1.title: Reading probe failures, continued
1.text: Reading probe failures. Running and zero slash one Ready means the readiness probe fails; Running with a rising restarts means liveness (or a crashing app). Fix the probe path, port or timing, or the app. Exam tip. A new Deployment whose Pods stay zero slash one for ever, with a probe on slash healthz for a web server that serves only or, is a classic "fix the probe" task. Check the real path with kube control exec pod then the command W get -q O- local host or.

1.title: API versions and deprecations
1.text: A P I versions and deprecations. Every object has an api Version made of a group and a version: apps slash version one, batch slash version one, networking dot K eights dot io slash version one; the core group is just version one. A version moves through stages. Alpha. Name looks like: version one alpha one. Meaning: off by default; may change or vanish. Beta. Name looks like: version one beta one. Meaning: on or off by default; may change. Stable (G A). Name looks like: version one. Meaning: kept for a long time. Exam tip: Find the correct api Version with kube control api resources, and remember that apps slash version one needs a spec dot selector.

1.title: API versions and deprecations, continued
1.text: A P I versions and deprecations. When a stable version replaces a beta version, the old one is deprecated (still served, with a warning) and later removed: a manifest that uses it fails with no matches for kind Cron Job in version batch slash version one beta one. Famous removals: extensions slash version one beta one and apps slash version one beta one Deployments, networking dot K eights dot io slash version one beta one Ingress (removed in one point two two), batch slash version one beta one Cron Job and policy slash version one beta one Pod Disruption Budget (removed in one point two five), autoscaling slash version two beta two H P A (removed in one point two six). Find the version the cluster serves.

1.title: API versions and deprecations, continued
1.text: A P I versions and deprecations. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: API versions and deprecations, continued
1.text: A P I versions and deprecations. Fix an old manifest. Change api Version, then apply what the new schema requires. For apps slash version one, spec dot selector is required and must match the Pod template labels (the beta versions defaulted it). For networking dot K eights dot io slash version one Ingress, path Type is required and the backend is service name, port number. Run kube control apply the dry run flag set to server dash f file dot yaml to check without creating.

1.title: API versions and deprecations, continued
1.text: A P I versions and deprecations. Warnings. kube control prints Warning... is deprecated when you use a deprecated A P I; the A P I server also exports metrics for deprecated calls. kube control convert is a separate plugin and is not part of the standard install, so do not count on it. Exam tip. For "this manifest fails", read the first line of the error: it names the kind and the version. Use kube control api resources to get the right api Version, then fix the fields the new version needs.

1.title: Lab 7.1: liveness exec
1.text: Lab seven point one: liveness exec. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod live in the namespace probes (manifest about slash work slash live dot yaml ) creates the file slash temp slash healthy, deletes it after fifteen seconds and keeps running. Add a liveness probe to its container that runs the command cat slash temp slash healthy every three seconds ( period Seconds three ) and treats two failures in a row as failed ( failure Threshold two ). Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. The kubelet must then restart the container at least once. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 7.1: liveness exec, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes delete pod live the wait flag set to true. cat about slash work slash live dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 7.1: liveness exec, Solution, continued
1.text: Lab seven point one: liveness exec, Solution, continued. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash live dot yaml. Then for i in seq one thirty do kube control dash n probes get pod live dash o json path dot status dot container Statuses zero dot restart Count -ge one two slash dev slash, and so on. Then kube control dash n probes describe pod live then pipe to grep dash i -A two Liveness.

1.title: Lab 7.2: fix readiness path
1.text: Lab seven point two: fix readiness path. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace probes, the Pods of the Deployment web (two replicas of engine X alpine, which serves its page at or ) never become Ready, because the readiness probe checks a path that does not exist. Fix the Deployment so that the readiness probe is an H T T P get on path or and port eighty, keep the probe, and wait until both replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.2: fix readiness path, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes describe pod dash l app web then pipe to grep dash i readiness. Then kube control dash n probes patch deployment web the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash readiness Probe slash H, and so on. Then kube control dash n probes rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.3: startup probe
2.text: Lab seven point three: startup probe. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod slow in the namespace probes (manifest about slash work slash slow dot yaml ) needs about twenty-five seconds to start, but its liveness probe starts checking after one second and keeps killing it. Without removing or loosening the liveness probe, add a startup probe to the container that runs the same command test dash f slash temp slash started every five seconds with failure Threshold twelve, so that the liveness probe only begins after the app has started. Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. It must become Ready with restart Count zero. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.3: startup probe, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes delete pod slow the wait flag set to true. cat about slash work slash slow dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.3: startup probe, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab seven point three: startup probe, Solution, continued. Run command sh, dash c, test dash f slash temp slash started. Then period Seconds five. Then failure Threshold twelve. Then liveness Probe. Then exec. Then command sh, dash c, test dash f slash temp slash started. Then initial Delay Seconds one. Then period Seconds two. Then failure Threshold two. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Lab 7.4: probe types
2.text: Lab seven point four: probe types. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace probes, create a Pod named api with one container (image engine X alpine ) that has a readiness probe of type T C P socket on port eighty ( initial Delay Seconds three, period Seconds five ) and a liveness probe of type H T T P get on path or and port eighty ( period Seconds ten, failure Threshold three ). Wait until the Pod is Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.4: probe types, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes run api the image flag set to engine X alpine the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml slash temp slash api dot yaml. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash api dot yaml. Then kube control dash n probes wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash api the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n probes describe pod api then pipe to grep -i E liveness then pipe to readiness. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.5: fix removed api versions
2.text: Lab seven point five: fix removed api versions. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The directory about slash work slash old holds three manifests written years ago: a Cron Job report, a Pod Disruption Budget web pdb and a Deployment web, all for the namespace legacy. kube control apply dash f about slash work slash old fails because they use A P I versions that the cluster no longer serves. Find the correct api Version for each kind (for example with kube control api resources and kube control explain ), fix the manifests (the Deployment also needs what its current A P I version requires), create the namespace legacy and apply all three. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.5: fix removed api versions, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns legacy. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash old two one then pipe to head -five. Then kube control api resources then pipe to grep -i E cronjobs then pipe to poddisruptionbudgets then pipe to deployments. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash old. Then kube control dash n legacy rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.6: find api versions
2.text: Lab seven point six: find api versions. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. Using only kube control against the cluster (no browser), write the current api Version of these four kinds to about slash answers slash apis dot txt, one line per kind in the form Kind api Version, sorted by kind name: Cron Job, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Ingress, Pod Disruption Budget. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.6: find api versions, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control api resources then pipe to head -three. Then for k in Cron Job Horizontal Pod Autoscaler Ingress Pod Disruption Budget do. Then kube control api resources the no headers flag awk dash v k k N F k print k, N F-two. Then done then pipe to sort about slash answers slash apis dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash apis dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a failing readiness probe do? Answer: The Pod is removed from the Service endpoints; the container is not restarted. Question two. What does a failing liveness probe do? Answer: The kubelet restarts the container. Question three. Why add a startup probe? Answer: So that a slow-starting app is not killed by the liveness probe before it has started.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which probe mechanisms exist? Answer: H T T P get, T C P socket, exec and G R P C. Question five. What status codes pass an H T T P probe? Answer: two hundred to three hundred ninety-nine. Question six. How do you find the api Version for a kind on your cluster? Answer: kube control api resources grep dash i kind (or kube control explain kind ).

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What does a removed A P I version produce? Answer: An error such as no matches for kind... in version... when you apply the manifest. Question eight. What must you add when you change a Deployment from apps slash version one beta one to apps slash version one? Answer: A spec dot selector that matches the Pod template labels.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Readiness: not ready: out of endpoints, no restart. Liveness: fails: container restarted. Startup: pauses the others until it passes; failure Threshold x period Seconds is the start budget. Mechanisms: H T T P get (two hundred to three hundred ninety-nine), T C P socket, exec (exit zero), G R P C. Defaults: period ten, timeout one, failure threshold three, success threshold one. Debug: describe pod events, logs the previous flag, get endpoints. A P I versions: api resources, api versions, explain; beta removed in later releases. Old manifest: new api Version plus required fields ( selector, path Type ).
